label: רבי אליעזר הגדול (רבי אליעזר בן הורקנוס)

questions.question: What did Rabbi Eliezer do when his brothers charged him with plowing rocky, hard ground?
options: He sat and wept over the plow, and finally fled to study in Jerusalem
He left home and engaged in the grain trade
He accepted the work in silence for many years
He hired workers in his place at his own expense
questions.explanation: He grew up as a farmhand without a Torah education. Out of longing for study, and after guidance from Elijah the Prophet, he fled to the yeshiva of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.

questions.question: According to the traditions, how long did Rabbi Eliezer go without tasting anything when he arrived in Jerusalem?
options: One day
Two Sabbaths, about two weeks
Forty days
A whole year
questions.explanation: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai noticed the smell of his mouth arising from hunger. Despite his poverty he persisted in his studies for three consecutive years.

questions.question: True or false: Hyrcanus went up to Jerusalem in order to give his son all his property.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: He went up in order to disinherit his son of his property. Only when he found him expounding before the great men of Jerusalem did he retract his vow.

questions.question: What did Rabbi Eliezer ask for when his father offered him all his property?
options: All the property, in order to dedicate it to the yeshiva
Nothing, because he gave up the inheritance
Only a portion equal to that of his brothers
Only the rocky land
questions.explanation: He refused to dispossess his brothers, even though they were the ones who had informed on him to their father.

questions.question: With what image did Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai describe Rabbi Eliezer?
options: An ever-strengthening spring
A threefold cord
One who uproots mountains
A plastered cistern that does not lose a drop
questions.explanation: The image describes a living archive of the tradition of the generations: he preserves the halakhot as he received them, without change, subtraction or addition.

questions.question: True or false: According to his approach, a sage may not rule a halakha that he did not hear from his teacher.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: This approach rejects the development of halakha on the basis of new analogies or pilpul.

questions.question: Who was Rabbi Eliezer's wife?
options: Imma Shalom, sister of Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh
Bruriah, daughter of Rabbi Chananiah ben Teradion
Yalta, wife of Rav Nachman
Rachel, daughter of Kalba Savua
questions.explanation: The marriage tied him directly to the patriarchal dynasty and to the central leadership of Yavneh.

questions.question: True or false: In Avot, Rabbi Eliezer said: "Warm yourself by the fire of the sages, and do not beware of their coals."
options: True
False
questions.explanation: He warned: "And beware of their coals, lest you be burned," for their bite is the bite of a fox, and all their words are like fiery coals.

questions.question: What was Rabbi Eliezer's position in the controversy over the Oven of Akhnai?
options: The oven is impure, because it serves as an oven in every respect
The oven is pure, because the sand between the segments separates them
The oven must be broken and rebuilt
No ruling should be made until Elijah comes
questions.explanation: In his view the oven is not a whole vessel but separate segments attached to the ground, and therefore it does not become impure. The Sages declared it impure.

questions.question: What signs did Rabbi Eliezer bring from heaven to prove that he was right?
options: An earthquake, lightning and rain in the summer
Fire from heaven that consumed the oven
A carob tree that was uprooted, water that flowed backward, and the walls of the study hall that began to tilt and fall
The sun standing still and a river drying up
questions.explanation: The Sages, led by Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hananiah, refused to recognize miracles as a means of halakhic decision.

questions.question: What did Rabbi Yehoshua answer the heavenly voice that said "The halakha follows him in every place"?
options: "We will do and we will hear"
"The halakha follows the House of Hillel"
"We have only the words of our teacher"
"It is not in heaven"
questions.explanation: Based on Deuteronomy 30:12. The Sages interpreted "follow the majority" as a basic constitutional law: the decision is given to the majority of the Sages.

questions.question: How did Rabbi Eliezer learn of his ban?
options: Rabbi Akiva, dressed in black, sat at a distance from him and said: "It seems to me that my colleagues are separating from you"
Rabban Gamliel sent him a letter
Rabbi Yehoshua announced it in the study hall in Lod
A heavenly voice informed him
questions.explanation: Many avoided approaching him because of his greatness, and Rabbi Akiva, his outstanding disciple, volunteered to inform him gently.

questions.question: True or false: When he said to the Roman judge "I trust the judge," Rabbi Eliezer meant the judge himself.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: He meant the Judge in heaven, out of acceptance of the judgment. The governor thought that he meant him, and acquitted him.

questions.question: What did Yaakov of Kfar Sechania ask Rabbi Eliezer in the upper marketplace of Sepphoris?
options: Whether it is permitted to pray in Greek
Whether it is permitted to build a privy for the High Priest from the hire of a prostitute
Whether it is permitted to offer sacrifices after the destruction
Whether it is permitted to marry a gentile woman
questions.explanation: Rabbi Eliezer enjoyed the interpretation "For from the hire of a prostitute she gathered them, and to the hire of a prostitute they shall return," and thereby transgressed "Keep your way far from her."

questions.question: True or false: Students of Torah through the generations, such as Rashi and the Rambam, attributed "Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer" to Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrcanus.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: From Rav Amram Gaon to the Ramban the work was attributed to the Tanna, although modern research dates it later.

questions.question: True or false: Rabbi Eliezer died while saying the word "pure."
options: True
False
questions.explanation: During his final illness in Caesarea the Sages asked him about impurity and purity. After his death the ban was lifted, and Rabbi Akiva eulogized him with bitter weeping.

questions.question: According to Rabbi Eliezer's homily, why is "with all your might" stated after "with all your soul"?
options: Because money is more important than the body to every person
Because money suffices to atone for idolatry
Because there is a person whose money is dearer to him than his body
Because one who gave his money is exempt from giving up his life
questions.explanation: One whose body is dear to him was commanded "with all your soul," and one whose money is dear to him "with all your might": one must give both body and money and not commit idolatry.

questions.question: According to the research, how are his words "I never said anything that I did not hear" reconciled with homilies "that no ear had heard"?
options: In his youth he innovated, and in his old age he retracted
He expounded his novel ideas only before his disciples
The novel ideas were those of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, and he merely transmitted them
Innovation, in his view, is the discovery of an ancient truth from Sinai that had been forgotten, not a human creation
questions.explanation: The sage, in his conception, is not a legislator but a clean conduit that restores divine knowledge that had been hidden from the people.

questions.question: What principle did the Sages establish in the controversy over the Oven of Akhnai, according to the research?
options: Since the giving of the Torah the decision is in the hands of the majority of the Sages, and no heavenly voice or miracle overrides it
The halakha follows the one who brings signs from heaven
In an evenly balanced dispute the Nasi decides
In the laws of impurity the halakha follows the House of Shammai
questions.explanation: Rabbi Eliezer saw halakha as a fixed divine truth; the Sages gave the study hall the authority to shape halakha.

questions.question: What did the scholar Zunz prove about "Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer"?
options: That Rabbi Eliezer wrote it in Lod in his old age
That the work was written in the eighth century and contains allusions to Islamic rule
That it was written in Babylonia in the days of Rav Ashi
That it was written in Spain in the twelfth century
questions.explanation: Among the evidence: criticism of the rule of the Ishmaelites and a mention of the Dome of the Rock. Nevertheless, the midrash preserves ancient traditions of the Land of Israel.
